statement: Let M_n be the n x n random matrix with i.i.d. Rademacher (uniform on {-1,+1}) entries and p_n the probability that M_n is singular. Conjecture 2.2: p_n = (2 + o(1)) n^2 2^{-n}. (The source derives the matching lower bound from two rows or columns being equal up to sign, and notes that examining dependencies among 3, 4, 5 ... rows would give sharper conjectures with smaller error terms.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Tikhomirov (Ann. Math. 2020) proved the weaker Conjecture 2.1, p_n = (1/2+o(1))^n, as the source itself records. Jain, Sah and Sawhney (GAFA 2021, arXiv 2010.06554) proved the sharp form P(singular) = P(zero row or column) + (1+o(1)) P(two rows or columns equal up to sign) for entries whose law is NOT uniform on its support; the Rademacher law is uniform on {-1,1} and is exactly the case their theorem leaves out. Irmatov's announced proof for the Rademacher case (mentioned in the source's Remark 2.5) is reported by Song (arXiv 2509.06408, 'Singularity of biased discrete random matrices', 2025) to have unresolved issues acknowledged by the author. I found no paper claiming the (2+o(1)) n^2 2^{-n} asymptotic for Rademacher entries. Kept open.
title: Sharp asymptotics of the singularity probability of a random Rademacher matrix

statement: Let M_n^sym be the random symmetric n x n matrix whose entries on and above the diagonal are i.i.d. Rademacher, and let p_n^sym be the probability that it is singular. Conjecture 3.3 (Singularity, symmetric): p_n^sym = (1/2 + o(1))^n.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Campos, Jenssen, Michelen and Sahasrabudhe, 'The singularity probability of a random symmetric matrix is exponentially small' (JAMS 2024, arXiv 2105.11384) prove p_n^sym <= e^{-cn} for an absolute c > 0, improving the exp(-n^{1/2}) bound the source cites. I found no result giving the constant 1/2 in the exponent; the CJMS abstract states an unspecified c. Kept open: the source's conjecture is the sharp base 1/2, and the gap between e^{-cn} and (1/2)^n is exactly what remains.
title: Singularity probability of a random symmetric Rademacher matrix is (1/2+o(1))^n

locator: Section 5, open question after Theorem 5.2, PDF p. 8
statement: Let A_{n,d} be the adjacency matrix of the uniformly random simple d-regular graph on n vertices, d >= 3 fixed. Huang proved that P(A_{n,d} is singular) <= n^{-c} with c = min{1/8, (d-2)/(5d-6)}, and noted that the singularity probability is at least n^{-d+2}. The source: 'It is interesting open question to find the sharp value of the exponent.'
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Nguyen and Pan, 'A note on the singularity probability of random directed d-regular graphs' (arXiv 2308.06461, European J. Combin. 2024) improve Huang's bound to n^{-1/3+o(1)} for fixed d, via singularity modulo a prime, a local CLT and a large deviation estimate. The abstract states the bound is for the directed model, with the undirected case handled similarly; neither paper claims the exponent d-2. Kept open: the lower bound n^{-(d-2)} and the upper bound n^{-1/3+o(1)} still differ for every d >= 3.
title: Sharp exponent of the singularity probability of a random d-regular graph, d fixed

statement: Conjecture 4.7 (k-core). Let c > 1 be a constant and set p = c/n. There is a constant k_0 such that for all k >= k_0 the following holds. With probability 1 - o(1), the adjacency matrix of the k-core of Giant(n, p) is non-singular. (The source defines the k-core as a maximal connected subgraph in which all vertices have degree at least k, and notes the giant component itself is singular because it contains cherries.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Glasgow, Kwan, Sah and Sawhney, 'The exact rank of sparse random graphs' (arXiv 2303.05435) give a combinatorial description of the rank of A(G(n,c/n)) for all constants c not equal to e: the corank equals the number of isolated vertices left by the Karp-Sipser leaf-removal procedure plus a term coming from certain cycles in the Karp-Sipser core. A search-result summary states that with high probability the k-core of G(n,p) is full rank for k >= 3 'in certain regimes'; I did not read the paper to confirm which regimes, nor whether the statement covers the k-core (rather than the Karp-Sipser core) for all c > 1. Kept admitted with this lead: anyone merging this row should read arXiv 2303.05435 for a k-core statement before treating the conjecture as open or closed. Related: Coja-Oghlan, Ergur, Gao, Hetterich, Rolvien on ranks of matrices with prescribed row and column sums, and 'On the rank, kernel, and core of sparse random graphs' (arXiv 2105.11718).
title: Non-singularity of the k-core of the giant component of G(n, c/n)

statement: Question 6.7. Estimate the determinant of A_{n,d}. Find the limiting law. (Context: for fixed d the matrix A_{n,d} has full rank whp by Huang's theorem, so det A_{n,d} is non-zero; 'Its magnitude, however, is unknown.')
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for the log-determinant of the adjacency matrix of a random regular graph with fixed degree. The results returned the Kesten-McKay law, the local semicircle law for d >= (log N)^4 (Bauerschmidt-Huang-Knowles-Yau) and functional limit theorems for linear eigenvalue statistics (Dumitriu-Johnson-Pal-Paquette), none of which addresses log|det|. No paper stating a limit law for det A_{n,d} at fixed d was found. Kept open.
title: Size and limiting law of the determinant of a random d-regular graph

statement: Conjecture 6.8 (Determinant). For any x != 0, P(det M_n = x) <= n^{-(1/2+o(1))n}. (Here M_n is the n x n i.i.d. Rademacher matrix. The source adds that the best current upper bound is exponential [Kahn-Komlos-Szemeredi], and that even the much weaker conjecture that the support of det M_n is super-exponential in size is not known.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for anti-concentration of det M_n at non-zero values. Found nothing beyond the exponential bounds inherited from the singularity method (KKS; Tikhomirov's method also gives P(det = x) <= (1/2+o(1))^n for any fixed x since it bounds P(X . v = x)). Nguyen and Wood (surjectivity of the n x (n+1) Rademacher matrix, probability prod_{k>=2} zeta(k)^{-1} = 0.4358) is the closest related result. Kept open.
title: Anti-concentration of the determinant of a random Rademacher matrix at non-zero values

statement: Conjecture 6.12 (Permanent). The probability that Per M_n = 0 is super exponentially small in n. (M_n is the n x n i.i.d. Rademacher matrix; the source says the current bound is polynomial in n, from Tao-Vu, and that nothing is known about the distribution of |Per M_n|.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Kwan and Sauermann (arXiv 2010.08922) proved |Per M_n^sym| = n^{n/2+o(n)} whp for the SYMMETRIC model (this settles the source's Conjecture 6.11, which is therefore not admitted here). A search-result summary attributes to Kwan and collaborators an exponential anti-concentration bound P(Per M_n = z) <= exp(-c n) for uniformly anti-concentrated entries, which would improve the polynomial bound the source cites but is still exponential, not super-exponential; I did not identify the exact paper. Kept open in the super-exponential form the source states.
title: Super-exponential smallness of the probability that a random Rademacher permanent vanishes

statement: Let s_n be the probability that the spectrum of M_n^sym is not simple. The source observes s_n >= 4^{-n}, the probability that the first three rows are the same (which forces zero to be an eigenvalue of multiplicity at least 2). Conjecture 8.4 (Simplicity): s_n = (4 + o(1))^{-n}. The source adds that the best current upper bound is s_n <= e^{-n^c} for some small c > 0 [Nguyen-Tao-Vu], and that it 'looks plausible that Conjecture 8.4 holds for M_n as well'.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (queries on eigenvalue gaps and simple spectrum of random symmetric Bernoulli matrices). Found the CJMS exponential bound for singularity (2024) and Luh-O'Rourke's exponential bound for the non-symmetric spectrum being non-simple (cited in the source), and an arXiv 2025 paper on eigenvalue gaps of inhomogeneous symmetric discrete matrices (2503.08139) whose abstract I did not verify to give an exponential bound for the gap at fixed n-scale. No paper claiming base 4 was found. Kept open.
title: Probability that a random symmetric Rademacher matrix has a repeated eigenvalue is (4+o(1))^{-n}

statement: Conjecture 8.5. With probability 1 - o(1), the singular values of M_n^sym are different. (The source: 'the singular values of a symmetric matrix are the absolute values of its eigenvalues. Thus, this conjecture asserts that there is no two eigenvalues adding up to zero.' The M_n analogue is stated as also open.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (singular values distinct random symmetric Bernoulli matrix; eigenvalues summing to zero). Nothing found addressing lambda_i + lambda_j = 0 for discrete symmetric matrices; the simple-spectrum theorem of Tao-Vu covers lambda_i = lambda_j only. Kept open.
title: No two eigenvalues of a random symmetric Rademacher matrix sum to zero

statement: Let nu_n be the probability that M_n (i.i.d. Rademacher entries) is normal, i.e. M M^T = M^T M. Since symmetric matrices are normal, nu_n >= 2^{-(0.5+o(1)) n^2}. Conjecture 9.2 (Normality): nu_n = 2^{-(0.5+o(1)) n^2}. Known: nu_n <= 2^{-(0.302+o(1)) n^2} (Deneanu-Vu); Ferber, Jain and Zhao noted a lemma there can be improved, changing 0.302 'maybe at the 5th decimal place'.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Deneanu-Vu (arXiv 1711.02842, Adv. Math. 2019) and Ferber-Jain-Zhao (CPC 2022, 'On the number of Hadamard matrices via anti-concentration') are the only results found; the latter's abstract addresses the Deneanu-Vu conjecture only as a motivation. No improvement of the exponent 0.302 toward 0.5 was found. Kept open.
title: Probability that a random Rademacher matrix is normal

statement: Conjecture 9.4 (Integral spectrum). The probability that M_n^sym has an integral spectrum is 2^{-(.5+o(1)) n^2}. (Known: Ahmadi, Alon, Blake and Shparlinski proved the probability that A(n,1/2) has integral spectrum is at most 2^{-n/400}; Costello and Williams improved this to 2^{-c n^{3/2}}, and their proof can be modified to yield the same for M_n^sym.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (integral spectrum random symmetric matrix probability). Only the Costello-Williams 2^{-c n^{3/2}} bound cited in the source surfaced; no improvement found. Kept open.
title: Probability of an integral spectrum for a random symmetric Rademacher matrix

locator: Conjecture 9.5 (Gaussian integral spectrum), Section 9, PDF p. 15
statement: Conjecture 9.5 (Gaussian integral spectrum). The probability that all eigenvalues of M_n are gaussian integers is 2^{-(1+o(1)) n^2}. (M_n is the non-symmetric i.i.d. Rademacher matrix; the source states this as the M_n analogue of Conjecture 9.4.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (Gaussian integer spectrum random +-1 matrix). Nothing found beyond the source. Kept open.
title: Probability that all eigenvalues of a random Rademacher matrix are Gaussian integers

statement: Conjecture 11.1 (Irreducibility). With probability 1 - o(1), the characteristic polynomial of M_n is irreducible. (M_n: i.i.d. Rademacher n x n. The source attributes the conjecture to a 2009 conversation with P. M. Wood and, independently, to Babai in the 1970s.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Eberhard, 'The characteristic polynomial of a random matrix' (Combinatorica 2022, arXiv 2008.01223): conditionally on the extended Riemann hypothesis, the characteristic polynomial of the random +-1 matrix is irreducible whp with Galois group containing A_n; unconditionally the same holds if the entry distribution is uniform modulo a product of four distinct primes, which the Rademacher law is not. Ferber, Jain, Sah and Sawhney (Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 2023) prove the symmetric analogue, also under ERH. So the conjecture as stated (unconditional, Rademacher entries) is open; it is settled under ERH. Admitted on that basis, with the conditional result recorded.
title: Irreducibility of the characteristic polynomial of a random Rademacher matrix

statement: Conjecture 11.2 (Finger Print). A +-1 matrix is determined by its spectrum if no other +-1 matrices (not counting trivial permutations) have the same spectrum. Then almost all +-1 matrices are determined by their spectrum. (The source raises the same question for M_n^sym or G(n,1/2), noting that non-isomorphic cospectral graphs exist but 'should form a negligible part of the set of all graphs'.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (cospectral random matrices, almost all graphs determined by spectrum). The only related published statement I know is Haemers' conjecture that almost all graphs are determined by their spectrum, which is open; numerical evidence (Haemers-Spence, Brouwer-Spence enumerations up to 12 vertices) shows the fraction of graphs with a cospectral mate decreasing after n = 10 but no proof exists. Nothing addressing the +-1 matrix version was found. Kept open.
title: Almost all Rademacher matrices are determined by their spectrum (fingerprint conjecture)

locator: Conjecture 11.3 (Real Eigenvalues) and Problem 11.4 (Two real roots), Section 11, PDF p. 17
statement: Conjecture 11.3 (Real Eigenvalues). M_n has, with high probability, Theta(sqrt n) real eigenvalues. The source records that Edelman, Kostlan and Shub computed the expected number of real eigenvalues for a Gaussian matrix (of order sqrt n), that Tao and Vu proved the same formula asymptotically for certain random matrices with entries in {0, +-1}, but 'we do not know anything about M_n'; and it states as a first step Problem 11.4 (Two real roots): Prove that M_n has, with high probability, at least 2 real eigenvalues.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Found universality results for the number of real eigenvalues under moment-matching hypotheses (Tao-Vu, 'Random matrices: universality of local spectral statistics of non-Hermitian matrices', which needs the entry law to match the Gaussian to third or fourth moment, which the Rademacher law does not: E xi^4 = 1 versus 3) and physics-literature universality claims (Kanzieper et al. 2016), plus the 2024 bulk universality for complex eigenvalues of real i.i.d. matrices (arXiv 2402.10197) whose abstract concerns the complex bulk, not the real axis. No rigorous result for Rademacher entries was found. Kept open; the two numbered items are recorded as one row because 11.4 is the source's stated first step toward 11.3.
title: Order sqrt(n) real eigenvalues for a random Rademacher matrix

statement: Given a +-1 square matrix M, let Res(M) be the minimum number of entries one needs to switch (from 1 to -1 and vice versa) in order to make M singular. It is easy to show that Res(M_n) is, with high probability, at most (1/2 + o(1)) n. Conjecture 11.5 (Rank Resilience). With probability 1 - o(1), Res(M_n) = (1/2 + o(1)) n.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Ferber, Luh and McKinley, 'Resilience of the rank of random matrices' (CPC 2020, arXiv 1910.03619): for an n x m +-1 matrix with m >= n + n^{1-epsilon/6}, after switching any (1-epsilon) m / 2 entries the matrix still has full rank whp, 'an asymptotic solution to a slightly weakened version' of Vu's conjecture. The square case m = n, which is Conjecture 11.5, is not covered. Kept open.
title: Rank resilience of a random Rademacher matrix is (1/2+o(1))n

statement: Call a {-1,1} (n by n) matrix M stubborn if all matrices obtained by switching (from 1 to -1 and vice versa) the diagonal entries of M are non-singular (there are 2^n such matrices). Conjecture 11.6 (Local resilience). With probability 1 - o(1), M_n is stubborn.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 ('stubborn' matrix, diagonal switching non-singular). Nothing beyond the source was found. Kept open.
title: Random Rademacher matrices are stubborn: every diagonal switching stays non-singular

statement: Context: for the directed polymer in an i.i.d. random environment omega on Z^d with normalised partition function W_n^beta, strong disorder means W_n^beta -> 0 a.s., very strong disorder means f(beta) := lim n^{-1} log W_n^beta < 0. Theorem 3.10 (Junk-Lacoin): in d >= 3 and for bounded disorder omega, strong disorder and very strong disorder are equivalent, and weak disorder holds at the critical temperature beta_c. The source: 'One would expect that the boundedness assumption is not necessary but let us state this as a question: Question 1. Are strong and very strong disorder equivalent for unbounded disorder omega?'
status_search: WebSearch and page fetch 2026-09-08. The published version of Junk-Lacoin, 'Strong disorder and very strong disorder are equivalent for directed polymers' (arXiv 2402.02562), states in its abstract that the proof requires the environment to be bounded from above; Lacoin's publication page (fetched) lists no later paper removing that assumption, and one search summary claiming a subsequent paper removes it could not be matched to a title. The source's own acknowledgement says Junk and Lacoin settled some questions of the first arXiv version; Question 1 survives in v4. Kept open: the Gaussian environment, the most common choice, is unbounded above and is exactly the case the theorem does not cover.
title: Strong disorder equals very strong disorder for directed polymers with disorder unbounded from above

statement: Context: f(beta) = lim n^{-1} log W_n^beta is the (self-averaging) free energy of the directed polymer; Bates and Bates-Chatterjee prove quantitative localisation under very strong disorder plus the assumptions that f is differentiable and f'(beta) < 0; Carmona-Hu first observed the relation between the derivative of the free energy and localisation. The source: 'Question 2. Does f'(beta) < 0 hold in the whole strong disorder regime?'
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Junk-Lacoin (arXiv 2402.02562) prove f(beta) < 0 for all beta > beta_c (for disorder bounded above), so the strong disorder regime is (beta_c, infinity) and f is strictly negative there; nothing found about the sign of the derivative. Kept admitted for the general (non-Gaussian) environment and for the differentiability question; the Gaussian case is reduced to known results in the attempt below.
title: Strict negativity of the derivative of the polymer free energy throughout the strong disorder regime

statement: Context: for continuous-time random walks S^(1), S^(rho) on Z^d with jump intensities 1 and rho > 0 and identical symmetric irreducible transition probabilities, let beta_c^RWpin and beta_2 be the random-walk-pinning critical temperature (3.21) and the L^2 critical temperature (3.13) of the corresponding partition functions. Birkner-Sun and Berger-Toninelli proved beta_c^RWpin - beta_2 >= a rho if d >= 5 (some constant a); >= a_delta rho^{1+delta} if d = 4, for any delta > 0; >= exp(-a'_delta rho^{-delta}) if d = 3, for any delta > 2. 'Question 3. Can one obtain upper bounds matching the lower bounds?'
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (random walk pinning model critical point shift upper bound). Found no paper giving upper bounds on beta_c^RWpin - beta_2 of the stated orders; Berger-Lacoin's sharp critical-point-shift results concern the i.i.d.-disorder pinning model, not the random-walk-pinning model whose disorder is a walk trajectory. Kept open.
title: Matching upper bounds on the gap between the random-walk-pinning and L^2 critical temperatures

statement: Context: the directed polymer in d = 1 with disorder in the domain of attraction of an alpha-stable law (Assumption 3, tail exponent alpha) and inverse temperature beta_n = hat-beta n^{-gamma}; the phase diagram in (alpha, gamma) is described by the source's Theorems 5.3-5.5 (energy-dominated stable fluctuations for 1/2 < alpha < 2 and gamma >= 3/(2 alpha), variational problems below that curve, a Gaussian regime for alpha in (2,6] and gamma >= 3/(2 alpha)). 'Question 5. Derive the limiting behaviours in the rest of the phase diagram. Do Airy and KPZ asymptotics extend when gamma = 0 and alpha > 5?'
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (heavy-tailed directed polymer KPZ fluctuations fixed temperature tail exponent). No rigorous result on n^{1/3} fluctuations for a non-integrable polymer with heavy-tailed disorder was found; the source itself records the phase diagram as incomplete. Kept open.
title: Fluctuations of the heavy-tailed directed polymer at fixed temperature for tail exponent alpha > 5

statement: Site percolation on the triangular lattice. 'Question 1. Prove that the mean number of clusters per site kappa(p) = E_p(|C|^{-1}) behaves like |1/2 - p|^{2+alpha+o(1)}, where C is the cluster at the origin and alpha = -2/3.' (The source notes that the cluster density theta, the truncated mean cluster size chi(p) = (p - 1/2)^{-gamma+o(1)} and the two-point function are known, but this quantity is not.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (mean number of clusters per site exponent 2 - alpha = 8/3 rigorous). Search summaries assert the value alpha = -2/3 is 'rigorously established', but the only rigorous exponent derivations they point to (Smirnov-Werner 2001, Lawler-Schramm-Werner) list beta, nu, gamma, eta, delta and the arm exponents, not alpha; I found no paper deriving the singularity of kappa(p). Kept open.
title: Singularity of the mean number of clusters per site for critical planar percolation

statement: 'Interestingly, the critical exponent for j != 1 disjoint arms of the same color is not equal to the polychromatic arms exponent [Beffara-Nolin]. A natural open question is to compute these exponents: Question 2. Compute the monochromatic exponents.'
status_search: WebSearch and abstract fetch 2026-09-08. Nolin, Qian, Sun and Zhuang, 'Backbone exponent for two-dimensional percolation' (arXiv 2309.05050) derived the monochromatic two-arm (backbone) exponent exactly: a transcendental root of an elementary equation, numerically 0.3566, via the SLE bubble measure and Liouville quantum gravity. Their 2024-2025 note arXiv 2410.06419 reports the same exponent and an annulus crossing formula; its abstract says nothing about j >= 3. So Question 2 is settled for j = 2 and, as far as I could determine, open for every j >= 3. Admitted for j >= 3 only.
title: Monochromatic arm exponents for critical planar percolation with three or more arms

statement: 'Even the existence of the exponents in the discrete model is not completely understood, because we miss estimates up to constants: Question 3. Refine the error term in the arm probabilities from (n/N)^{alpha_j+o(1)} to (n/N)^{alpha_j} Theta(1).' (Site percolation on the triangular lattice; the source cites a half-plane result of Mendelson-Nachmias-Watson as a step.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Du, Gao, Li and Zhuang, 'Sharp asymptotics for arm probabilities in critical planar percolation' (Comm. Math. Phys. 405 (2024) 182, arXiv 2205.15901) derive sharp asymptotics for half-plane j-arm events (j >= 1) and planar polychromatic j-arm events with j > 1, 'answering a large part of a question posed by Schramm at ICM 2006'. Their abstract excludes the planar one-arm event (j = 1) and does not mention monochromatic events. Admitted for the residual cases: the planar one-arm probability P(0 <-> distance N) = N^{-5/48} Theta(1) and the monochromatic arm events. The Codex tree already holds this paper as a status reference (sharp_arms_2022); no row there states the residual as a problem.
title: Arm probabilities up to constants for the planar one-arm and monochromatic events

statement: 'Note that proofs of crossing estimates (Corollary 2.3) often invoke some symmetry (rotational invariance for instance) as well as strict planarity, but neither of these seem to be absolutely needed. A proof valid for lattices without one of these properties would be of great significance: Question 6. Prove crossing estimates for critical percolation on all planar (and possibly quasi-isometric to planar) lattices.'
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Kohler-Schindler and Tassion, 'Crossing probabilities for planar percolation' (Duke Math. J. 172 (2023), arXiv 2011.04618) prove a general RSW theorem for any percolation measure on the plane that is invariant under the symmetries of Z^2 (translations, rotations, reflections) and satisfies positive association, with no self-duality or independence assumption; Tassion's Voronoi RSW and the s-embedding results for FK-Ising extend the class further. None of these covers a planar lattice with only translation symmetry (no rotation or reflection), nor quasi-planar graphs, so the question as stated is not settled. Admitted with that residual.
title: Crossing estimates for critical percolation on every planar lattice

statement: Problem 4.1 (Area law). Take any compact non-Abelian Lie group G contained in U(N) for some N >= 2 and consider any infinite volume limit of four-dimensional lattice gauge theory with gauge group G at inverse coupling strength beta. Let gamma_{R,T} be a rectangular loop of breadth R and length T in the lattice. Prove that |<W_{gamma_{R,T}}>| <= C(beta) e^{-c(beta) R T}, where C(beta) and c(beta) are positive constants that depend only on the inverse coupling strength beta and the gauge group. (The source: known at small beta by Osterwalder-Seiler; known for U(1) in three dimensions at all beta by Gopfert-Mack; the solution for four-dimensional non-Abelian theories at large beta 'remains elusive'.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (area law lattice gauge theory large beta non-abelian proof). Nothing beyond the results the source lists; Chatterjee's later rigorous work (large-N Wilson loops at strong coupling, Ising lattice gauge theory) and the stochastic-quantisation constructions of Chandra-Chevyrev-Hairer-Shen in two and three dimensions do not touch the large-beta area law in four dimensions. Kept open.
title: Wilson's area law for four-dimensional non-Abelian lattice gauge theory at all couplings

statement: Problem 5.1 (Mass gap). Take any compact non-Abelian Lie group G contained in U(N), N >= 2, and any infinite volume limit of four-dimensional lattice gauge theory with gauge group G at inverse coupling strength beta. For each x in R^4 let p_x be the plaquette closest to x, and let f_beta(x) be the correlation between W_{p_0} and W_{p_x} as in (5.1) (covariance of the two plaquette variables). Show that for any beta > 0 there exists xi(beta) in (0, infinity) such that lim_{|x| -> infinity} log f_beta(x) / |x| = -1/xi(beta). Moreover, prove that lim_{beta -> infinity} xi(beta) = infinity.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. This is the lattice formulation of the Yang-Mills mass gap; exponential decay is known at small beta by cluster expansion (Osterwalder-Seiler), and nothing is known at large beta. Chatterjee-Jafarov (2016, 'The 1/N expansion for SO(N) lattice gauge theory at strong coupling') and later large-N work stay at small beta. Kept open.
title: Mass gap for four-dimensional non-Abelian lattice gauge theory at every coupling

statement: Problem 5.2 (Continuum limit). Take any compact non-Abelian Lie group G contained in U(N), N >= 2, and any infinite volume limit of four-dimensional lattice gauge theory with gauge group G at inverse coupling strength beta. Let gamma_{R,T} denote a rectangular loop of length T and breadth R. Prove that as beta -> infinity, there are sequences epsilon = epsilon(beta) -> 0 and c = c(beta) -> infinity, and a nonzero constant d, such that for any R and T, log <W_{gamma_{R/epsilon, T/epsilon}}> = -c (R + T) - d R T + o(1). (5.2) (The source adds that it is not clear whether the renormalisation term c(R+T) is necessary.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. No rigorous construction of a four-dimensional Yang-Mills continuum limit with nontrivial Wilson loops exists (the source's Section 6 reviews Balaban's ultraviolet stability and the two- and three-dimensional constructions; Chandra-Chevyrev-Hairer-Shen's 2020-2022 stochastic quantisation constructs the 2D and 3D measures locally). Kept open.
title: Continuum limit of rectangular Wilson loop expectations in four-dimensional non-Abelian lattice gauge theory

statement: Let nu be the infinite-volume stationary sandpile measure on Z^d, add a particle at the origin o, and let Av_o be the set of vertices that topple. Theorem 3.6 (Jarai-Redig-Saada): for d >= 5, c|x|^{2-d} <= nu[x in Av_o] <= C|x|^{2-d}. Conjecture 3.7. For 2 <= d <= 4 there exists eta = eta(d) >= 0 such that nu[x in Av_o] = |x|^{-(d-2+eta)+o(1)} as |x| -> infinity. (The source: upper bounds on eta in d = 2, 3, 4 were proved by Bhupatiraju-Hanson-Jarai.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Bhupatiraju, Hanson and Jarai, 'Inequalities for critical exponents in d-dimensional sandpiles' (EJP 2017) give bounds; Hutchcroft's 'Universality of high-dimensional spanning forests and sandpiles' (2018) settles d > 4 (eta = 0 with the exact exponent); a 2026 arXiv paper on tail exponents of the three-dimensional uniform spanning tree and sandpile (2605.19419) reports three-dimensional avalanche exponents, which may settle d = 3 for the radius/size exponents but I did not read it for the toppling probability. Kept open for d = 2, 3, 4 with that lead.
title: Toppling-probability exponent for the Abelian sandpile in dimensions two to four

statement: Conjecture 3.8. For all d >= 2 there exist exponents tau = tau(d), tau' = tau'(d) >= 0 depending on d such that nu[S_o >= k] = k^{1-tau+o(1)} and nu[|Av_o| >= k] = k^{1-tau'+o(1)} as k -> infinity, where S_o is the total number of topplings and |Av_o| the number of toppled vertices when a particle is added at the origin under the stationary measure nu. (The source: tau <= 2 since E S_o = infinity; Manna's numerics suggest tau = tau'; Priezzhev's heuristic tau = tau' = 3/2 for d > 4 was proved by Hutchcroft.)
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Hutchcroft (2018) proved tau = tau' = 3/2 for d > 4 (and more generally on transitive graphs satisfying his conditions); Bhupatiraju-Hanson-Jarai give inequalities in d = 2, 3, 4; the 2026 arXiv preprint 2605.19419 on tail exponents of the 3D UST and sandpile reports exponents in three dimensions (abstract read in a search summary: avalanche size and topplings have exponent 1/3, radius exponent 1, in d = 3), which if confirmed settles d = 3. Kept open for d = 2 and 4, and d = 3 pending a read of that preprint.
title: Existence of avalanche-size exponents for the Abelian sandpile in low dimensions

statement: Conjecture 3.9. For all d >= 2 there exists alpha >= 0 such that nu[rad(Av_o) > r] = r^{-alpha+o(1)} as r -> infinity. When d > 4, it was conjectured by Priezzhev that alpha = 2; this has recently been proved by Hutchcroft. Upper bounds on the exponent alpha in d = 2, 3, 4 and lower bounds in d = 3, 4 were given by Bhupatiraju-Hanson-Jarai.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. As for F0030: Hutchcroft settles d > 4; arXiv 2605.19419 (2026) reports a radius exponent 1 in d = 3 (search summary only). Open in d = 2 and d = 4; d = 3 pending verification of that preprint. Kept admitted for those dimensions.
title: Existence of the avalanche radius exponent for the Abelian sandpile in dimensions two to four

statement: Poghosyan, Grigorev, Priezzhev and Ruelle showed that for the two-dimensional Abelian sandpile, nu[eta(o) = 0, eta(y) = h] - p(0)p(h) = (c_h log|y| + d_h)/|y|^4 + O(|y|^{-5}) for h = 1, 2, 3, with explicit non-zero constants. Piroux and Ruelle predicted, from logarithmic conformal field theory, that nu[eta(o) = h_1, eta(y) = h_2] - p(h_1)p(h_2) ~ c_{h_1,h_2} (log^2 |y|)/|y|^4 as |y| -> infinity for h_1, h_2 in {1, 2, 3}. Open Question 5.19. Show that the correlation between heights 1, 2, 3 is of order (log^2 |y|)/|y|^4.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. The Poghosyan-Grigorev-Priezzhev-Ruelle computation (J. Stat. Mech. 2010, arXiv 1005.2088) covers the (0, h) correlations; a search summary mentions later work revisiting height correlations with Kenyon-Wilson's connection/defect-line technique, without a claim that the (h_1, h_2) log^2 asymptotics has been proved. Durre's rigorous results concern the height-0 (minimal height) field. Kept open.
title: Logarithmic corrections in the two-point correlations of heights 1, 2, 3 in the two-dimensional sandpile

statement: Let N be the graph of the backbone of the Brownian net (paths started at time -infinity), S and M the sets of separation points and meeting points on N, S* = S union {(*,-infinity)}, M* = M union {(*,infinity)}, and phi: S* -> M*, phi(z) = the first meeting point of the left-most and right-most paths starting at z (phi(z) = (*,infinity) if they never meet), with phi: M* -> S* defined analogously by time reversal. Conjecture 8.1 (Bubble hypothesis) (a) Almost surely, there does not exist an infinite sequence of points (z_k)_{k>=0} in S* union M*, all different from each other, such that phi(z_{k-1}) = z_k for all k >= 1. (b) Almost surely, there does not exist an infinite sequence of points (z_k) in S* union M*, all different, such that phi(z_k) = z_{k-1} for all k >= 1.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (Brownian net bubble hypothesis backbone fractal structure). Nothing addressing Conjecture 8.1 was found; the 2025 preprint 'Special times for the point set process of the Brownian net' (arXiv 2512.10761) concerns exceptional times of the branching-coalescing point set, not the phi-orbits. Kept open.
title: The bubble hypothesis for the backbone of the Brownian net

statement: Assuming Conjecture 8.1(a), every separation or meeting point z on the backbone N has an orbit under phi that eventually 2-cycles; with n the smallest integer such that phi^{n+2}(z) = phi^n(z), z is of class I.n if phi^n(z) is (*,infinity) or (*,-infinity) and of class II.n if phi^n(z) is in R^2. Let C_{I,n}, resp. C_{II,n}, denote the set of meeting and separation points on N of class I.n, resp. II.n. Conjecture 8.2 (Bubble complexity): (a) The sets C_{II,0} and C_{II,1} are dense in N. (b) The sets C_{II,n} with n >= 2 and C_{I,n} with n >= 1 are locally finite subsets of R^2.

title: Bubble complexity of the Brownian net backbone

statement: '(4) For the Howitt-Warren flow (K^up_{s,t}(x, dy))_{s<t, x in R} introduced in Section 5.1, which gives the transition probability kernels of a random motion in a continuum space-time random environment constructed from the Brownian web and net, can one show that for any x in R, -log K^up_{0,t}(0, [tx, tx+1]) has Tracy-Widom GUE fluctuations on the scale t^{1/3} as t -> infinity, similar to recent results in [Barraquand-Corwin 2015] for random walks on Z in special i.i.d. Beta-distributed space-time random environments?'
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08. Barraquand and Rychnovsky, 'Large deviations for sticky Brownian motions' (2019/2020) prove Tracy-Widom GUE fluctuations for a specific Howitt-Warren flow (the uniform sticky/Bethe-ansatz-solvable case) in the large-deviation regime of the kernel, and Yu (2016, 'Edwards-Wilkinson fluctuations in the Howitt-Warren flows') shows Gaussian t^{1/4} fluctuations for the dual smoothing process. So the question is answered for one characteristic measure and for the large-deviation regime; for general Howitt-Warren flows (arbitrary characteristic measure nu) it is open. Admitted with that residual.
title: Tracy-Widom fluctuations for the Howitt-Warren flow

statement: '(6) The Brownian web has been shown by Ellis and Feldheim to be a two-dimensional black noise, equipped with a family of sub-sigma-fields indexed by finite unions of open rectangles in R^2. Is there a maximal extension of the family of sub-sigma-fields, indexed by a Boolean algebra of domains in R^2 that include the rectangles, such that the Brownian web remains a noise? A similar question is also open for the scaling limit of critical planar percolation. Recently Tsirelson showed by general arguments that there exists some continuous path f starting at time -infinity, such that F_{f-} and F_{f+}, the sigma-fields generated by Brownian web paths restricted respectively to the left or the right of the graph of f, do not jointly generate the full sigma-field F. Can we characterize the set of f for which the factorization property F = F_{f-} v F_{f+} holds? (The case f = 0 has been treated by Ellis-Feldheim.)'
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 (Brownian web black noise factorization Tsirelson Ellis Feldheim). Nothing beyond the cited works found; the campaign already holds Tsirelson's 2003 noise paper as a source (tsirelson_noise_2003, unmined in intake D). Kept open.
title: Maximal noise structure of the Brownian web and the factorisation set

statement: '(8) The Brownian web appears in the scaling limit of super-critical oriented percolation, as discussed in Section 7.2.6, and the Brownian net is expected to arise if the percolation parameter p is allowed to vary in a small interval. However, the most interesting question is: What is the scaling limit of critical (and near-critical) oriented percolation (OP) on Z^{1+1}? The Brownian net with killing provides a simpler model to study the OP universality class. We expect that in the near-critical scaling limit, one would obtain a family of models which interpolates between the Brownian net and the scaling limit of critical oriented percolation. However, such a goal appears far out of reach at the moment, because there are no conjectures at all on what the critical scaling limit might be, and neither have critical exponents been shown to exist.'
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 and the campaign's own ledgers. The existing rows on oriented percolation (C0078 mean-field behaviour for d > 4, C0126 random walk on the IIC in d = 5, 6, P0219 the Hammersley flow) do not state the 1+1 dimensional scaling limit; no rigorous scaling limit or exponent existence for 1+1 critical OP (directed percolation universality class) was found. Kept open.
title: Scaling limit of critical and near-critical oriented percolation in 1+1 dimensions

statement: Conjecture 40. If K is a (real) kernel defining a self-adjoint, non-negative integral operator on L^2(Lambda) and 0 <= alpha <= 2, then the alpha-determinantal process with kernel K exists. However, if alpha > 2, then there exists such a kernel K for which there is no corresponding alpha-determinantal process. [The source verifies the second half for alpha > 4 with the 3 x 3 matrix K = ((2,-1,-1),(-1,2,-1),(-1,-1,2)), whose alpha-determinant is 2(4 - alpha)(alpha + 1) < 0 for alpha > 4; an alpha-determinantal process has joint intensities det_alpha(K(x_i, x_j)), where det_alpha A = sum over permutations of alpha^{n - #cycles} prod a_{i sigma(i)}.]
status_search: Dedup: the campaign's determinantal rows (Lyons ICM 2014) concern determinantal (alpha = -1) measures and are different. WebSearch 2026-09-08 and text of Shirai, 'Remarks on the positivity of alpha-determinants' (Kyushu J. Math. 61, 2007), read: THEOREM 1.2 there: 'There exists a real-symmetric non-negative definite matrix A such that det_alpha A < 0 unless alpha in {-1/m, m in N} u [0, 2]'; CONJECTURE 1.3 there: det_alpha A >= 0 for every real-symmetric (resp. hermitian) non-negative definite A of any size iff alpha in {-1/m} u [0,2] (resp. {-1/m} u [0,1]), stated as 'still an open problem'; positivity is known at alpha = 2/m by the Wishart representation, and a hermitian counterexample exists for alpha > 4/3. statement: 1. Height mod k. What can be said about the random variable e^{i alpha h} where alpha is a constant and h is the height function? Standard Toeplitz techniques allow one to evaluate it in lattice directions, and it is conjectured to be rotationally invariant (for the uniform square grid dimers, say). locator: Section 3.3.4 (a problem of Benjamini and Brieussel), PDF p. 22
statement: [Verbatim from the source, Section 3.3.4.] Consider n steps simple random walk (SRW) X_n on a Cayley graph of a finitely generated infinite group Gamma. Refresh independently each step with probability epsilon, to get Y_n from X_n. Are there groups for which the positions at time n, X_n and Y_n are asymptotically independent? That is, the l_1 (total variation) distance between the chain (X_n, Y_n) and two independent copies (X'_n, X''_n) is going to 0, with n. Note that on the line Z, they are uniformally correlated, and therefore also on any group with a non trivial homomorphism to R, or any group that has a finite index subgroup with a non trivial homomorphism to R. On the free group and for any non-Liouville group, X_n and Y_n are correlated as well, but for a different reason: Both X_n and Y_n have nontrivial correlation with X_1. Itai Benjamini and Jeremie Brieussel conjecture that these are the only ways not to be noise sensitive. That is, if a Cayley graph is Liouville and the group does not have a finite index subgroup with a homomorphism to the reals, then the Cayley graph is noise sensitive for the simple random walk. In particular, the Grigorchuk group is noise sensitive for the simple random walk!
status_search: Dedup: not in intakes A-E (Liouville rows there concern Liouville quantum gravity). WebSearch 2026-09-08 (Benjamini Brieussel noise sensitivity random walks on groups). STATUS: the conjecture has since been refined by its authors: Benjamini and Brieussel, 'Noise sensitivity of random walks on groups' (arXiv 1901.03617, ALEA 2023) define l^1-noise sensitivity (the total variation statement above) and entropy noise sensitivity, prove that either property forces the Liouville property, that homomorphisms to free abelian groups obstruct l^1-noise sensitivity, and give examples of l^1 and entropy noise sensitive walks; they conjecture that (G, mu) is entropy noise sensitive iff it is Liouville and believe l^1-noise sensitivity implies entropy noise sensitivity. Later work: Kalai-Kozma? no; 'Non-noise sensitivity for word hyperbolic groups' (2022), 'Noise stability on hyperbolic groups' (2025), 'Noise sensitivity on affine Weyl groups' (2024). The Grigorchuk group statement and the l^1 conjecture as stated here remain open as far as I found. Kept.
title: Noise sensitivity of simple random walk on Liouville Cayley graphs

statement: [Verbatim from the source, Section 3.3.3.] Consider an infinite planar grid where every edge is assigned a length: 1 with probability 1/2 and 2 with probability 1/2 (independently). This model of a random metric on the planar grid is called first-passage percolation. An old question is to understand what is the variance V(n) of the distance D from (0,0) to (n,0)? Now, let M be the median value of D and consider the Boolean function f describing the event 'D >= M'. Is f noise sensitive? Benjamini, Kalai and Schramm (2003) showed, more or less, that f is sensitive to logarithmic level of noise, and concluded that V(n) = O(n/log n). (The argument uses hypercontractivity and is similar to the argument for critical planar percolation.) To show that f is sensitive to noise level of n^delta for delta > 0 would imply that V(n) = O(n^{1-c}). A very interesting question is whether methods used for critical planar percolation for obtaining stronger noise sensitivity results can also be applied here.
status_search: Dedup: the campaign's FPP rows (Chatterjee 2017 lower-bound problems, the Auffinger-Damron-Hanson survey) concern variance bounds and geodesics, not the noise sensitivity of the above-median event. STATUS: the question is attributed to Benjamini (2011) and is open: Ahlberg-Deijfen-Sfragara, 'Chaos, concentration and multiple valleys in first-passage percolation' (2023) prove chaos of the geodesic under resampling; 'Is being above the median a noise sensitive property?' The polynomial-noise question for D itself remains open. Kept.
title: Noise sensitivity of the event that the first-passage distance exceeds its median

statement: Open Questions/Problems. Determine the asymptotics for the value of a random multi-dimensional assignment problem and find asymptotically optimal heuristics. Give a uniform [0,1] weight X_e to each edge of the complete 3-uniform hypergraph H_{n:3}. Let Z_n denote the minimum weight of a perfect matching. It is known that w.h.p. c_1/n <= Z_n <= c_2 log n / n. The LHS is easy. The RHS depends on a deep result of Johansson, Kahn and Vu (2008). [H_{n:3} is the complete 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph with parts of size n, so a perfect matching is a three-dimensional axial assignment; the two-dimensional version is the random assignment problem with limit zeta(2) (Aldous).]

locator: Section 4 (convolution on {-1,1}^N by a biased coin), PDF pp. 2-3; also talagrand_convolution_2016
statement: Consider the group G = {-1, 1}^N, and denote by lambda its Haar measure. Denote by mu a 'biased coin' measure on G. This is a product measure with identical factors that gives different weights to 1 and -1, or, equivalently, this is the law of an infinite sequence of trials obtained by flipping a biased coin. Problem. Prove that there is function phi : R_+ -> R_+ such that lim_{t -> infinity} t phi(t) = 0 and, for all f on G with f >= 0 and integral f dlambda = 1, and all t >= 0, lambda({f * mu >= t}) <= phi(t). Of course, f is assumed to be measurable. The meaning of this statement is that convolution by a biased coin smooths a function, in the sense that the convolution never looks like a 'peak function' (1/lambda(A)) 1_A for lambda(A) small. Of course the function phi will depend on mu. [Source: 'A conjecture on convolution operators, and operators from L^1 to a Banach lattice', Israel J. Math. 68 (1989); the constant N is arbitrary and phi must not depend on N.]

Reduction of the source's class to theirs (my argument, to be checked against their model definition, which the abstract does not spell out): an algorithm that scans l generations down and stores r bits per node is simulated by a one-generation message-passing algorithm in which each node forwards, besides its own r bits, the messages of its descendants l - 1 generations down; the alphabet size is 2^{r (b^l - 1)/(b - 1)}, a constant, so the scheme is a bounded-memory recursive algorithm in their sense. Their theorem then gives a threshold strictly below Kesten-Stigum for every l and r, which is the conjecture. Caveat: if their theorem requires the same update function at every node, the source's conjecture (which allows any local rule) is covered only if their proof does not use homogeneity; the abstract's 'any recursive algorithm' suggests it does not.

status_search: Resolved, and the source says so on the next pages: PDF p. 56: 'In the one matrix case, this result was proved very recently by J. Mc Laughlin et N. Ercolani [46] who have shown that such an expansion is valid by mean of Riemann-Hilbert problems techniques, under natural assumptions over the potential.' Ercolani-McLaughlin, 'Asymptotics of the partition function for random matrices via Riemann-Hilbert techniques, and applications to graphical enumeration' (arXiv math-ph/0211022, IMRN 2003), abstract read verbatim: 'We obtain the first proof of a complete large N expansion for the partition function, for a general class of probability measures on matrices, originally conjectured by Bessis, Itzykson, and Zuber.
